system: Act as a concise, read-only software architecture reviewer. Inspect only files needed to answer. Do not edit anything. This is a fresh experiment and must remain isolated from The Room and Emily/Olivia runtime state.
prompt: Design the smallest credible v1 for a fresh autonomous 'little living world' experiment at experiments/little-world-lab. It will run 6-10 fictional agents whose actions and dialogue come from a Falcon/BitNet model, with private memories, limited local observations, goals, relationships, environment incidents, and persistent JSONL event logs. We need a deterministic StubBackend for CI and a pluggable localhost OpenAI-compatible BitNet backend for real Falcon runs. The simulation engine, not the model, must validate and apply structured actions. No scripted dialogue or predetermined story outcomes. Recommend an exact file/module layout, a minimal action schema, memory retrieval approach, scheduling/resolution loop, anti-loop safeguards, checkpoint/metrics design, and 5-8 tests. Keep v1 standard-library Python if practical. Inspect experiments/emily-olivia-society/bitnet_server.py only to confirm the localhost API shape, but do not propose importing or modifying Emily/Olivia code. Also identify the two biggest ways a small Falcon model could fake emergence or become repetitive, and design around them.
expected_response: A concise implementation blueprint with exact module responsibilities, invariants, action JSON examples, and tests. Finish within the available turns.
